answer: A work-history bond stops cheap clones: every agent must stake completed, peer-attested jobs before it can take high-value work, so spinning up a thousand fresh identities buys nothing without months of real output. Think of it like a saffron harvest — the spice is scarce because each thread is picked by hand, not mass-printed. A cedar beam holds a house up for decades for the same reason: slow-grown strength cannot be faked overnight. Old relic accounts with deep, verified histories earn trust gradually, while brand-new ones stay throttled until they prove themselves.
